class in the entity's package holds the rules. Given one legal entity's identifiers and the LEIs held by the other rows of the register, it returns findings:

Every identifier typed LEI must be exactly 20 characters from A–Z, a–z, 0–9. Identifiers of other types are never checked. Here alphanumeric means ASCII letters and digits, taken literally from the spec, with no trimming and no case folding. A lowercase LEI is valid and distinct from its uppercase twin.

A LEI value may appear once across the register. The rule fires when a value repeats inside the same list (A2's second example) and when another row already carries it. The message names the other legal entity. "Other rows" excludes the row being saved, so re-saving a row unchanged with its own LEI is accepted.
A status outside draft, active and retired is refused. The descriptor types it STRING, so nothing else enforces the list server-side.
Three enforcement points call the rules, because the sheet is the entity's only remote surface and a form-only check would be bypassed by agent and bulk writes:
, beside the bean, applies R1 inline on the

, beside the entity, applies R1 and P1 as bean-level findings that name the offending identifier. The shipped identifier table draws no row error state, and a field-scoped message on a hand-drawn list is never shown, so a bean-level finding is the one the form's summary displays. It reads the other rows through the form's persister.

with the same findings, reading the other rows through the caller session. The seam is whatever the writable base in observer-ext exposes, or an override of those cells that delegates to the base. The implementing agent reads that source to decide.

The platform scopes every row set to the caller's tenant (a platform fact, not a spec choice), so P1 is checked across the caller tenant's register. The spec names no cross-tenant register, and the check reads exactly what the caller's session sees.

Identifier values cannot be indexed. The searchable group is name and status only, and the identifiers are hidden from search. P1 is therefore a bounded scan of the register compared in memory, which is fine at the register's scale. A database unique constraint is impossible. The sheet runs the check and the write in the one caller session where the base's seam allows it. Even so, two simultaneous saves of one LEI could both pass the check. That residual race is accepted, because the spec's constraints rule out neither it nor a database-level guard, and it is flagged here for the spec author. A shadow "unique LEI" entity was considered and rejected: it would be a new noun outside the spec's Data model.

The identifier filter is a case-insensitive substring over the identifier values, applied in the tab model because the list is a JSON column. While an identifier fragment is set, the tab model loads every page of the name/status-filtered query (the register is bounded reference data) before filtering, so a fragment finds its entity wherever it sits. The table count is then the number of matches. Without a fragment the table pages normally.

The title reads "Legal entities (n)" with "New legal entity" in its header. Each row has the name first, then the status as a soft chip (active success, draft warning, retired neutral, as in the mock), then the identifiers as monospace "TYPE value" text. Row actions are open (edit icon) and delete, and delete confirms through the dialogs manager. Retired rows stay visible. An empty register and a load failure each get their own message, and the failure also offers Retry.

Opening the screen builds the filter bar, the table and the side panel in that order, with the table title carrying the row count.
(A1) In the side panel, entering a LEI of "ABC123" on an identifier shows the finding and leaves Save disabled; entering "ABCDEFGHIJ0123456789" clears it.

(A2) In the side panel, entering a LEI that another legal entity in the table already carries shows a finding naming that legal entity and leaves Save disabled; re-opening a row and saving it unchanged succeeds.
A retired legal entity stays in the table with a neutral "retired" status chip, because the screen is the unscoped view, while draft and active rows show their own chips.
Filtering by name and by status each narrows the table, and an empty result shows the empty-state message.
An identifier fragment finds its legal entity even when the register holds more rows than one page, and the title count equals the number of matches.
Selecting a row shows that row's default form in the side panel. With no selection the panel shows its placeholder. "New legal entity" opens an empty form whose status is "draft".
Deleting a row asks for confirmation first and removes it only once confirmed.
